description: We are a team of four passionate individuals bringing together interests in physics, artificial intelligence, and software development. With strengths in classical physics, advanced scientific studies, AI-based coding, and problem-solving, we aim to combine scientific thinking with modern technology. We believe in collaboration, creativity, and innovation, and are eager to transform ideas into practical solutions that address real-world challenges.
summary: Nebula Core: The Last Days of Opportunity is an advanced, data-driven mission control web dashboard honoring NASA’s dormant Mars Exploration Rover, Opportunity (MER-B). Built for the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, the platform transforms raw historical mission records into an immersive, interactive experience. It features an interactive Leaflet.js geospatial map tracking Meridiani Planum waypoints (Eagle Crater, Endurance, Victoria, Endeavour, and Perseverance Valley), time-series Chart.js telemetry graphs analyzing 5,111 Sols of battery degradation, a multi-act first-person narrative chronicling the rover's 14-year legacy, and a live physics simulator driven by real atmospheric dust optical depth (tau) equations. Nebula Core bridges deep space telemetry with emotional storytelling, serving as a permanent digital monument to humanity's most resilient robotic geologist on Mars.
details:
What it does & How it works:

Nebula Core is a full-stack Django mission control web application designed to track, visualize, and memorialize NASA’s Opportunity Rover. It ingests authentic historical Mars Exploration Rover (MER-B) datasets into an optimized SQLite database via custom management commands. The frontend features a dual-panel command center:

1. Geospatial Map & Timeline: An interactive Leaflet.js map centered on Meridiani Planum, mapping Opportunity's exact landing site (-1.9547° S, 354.4734° E) and historical craters.

2. Telemetry & Physics Engine: Real-time Chart.js graphs displaying multi-row time-series metrics (battery watt-hours, board temperatures, and dust optical depth over 5,111 Sols) coupled with an interactive dust storm simulator calculating solar power decay based on the Beer-Lambert law.

3. Rover's Voice: A 3-act first-person narrative chronicle detailing its 2004 touchdown, scientific discoveries, and final transmission on June 10, 2018.

Benefits & Impact:

The platform preserves space history, makes complex planetary science data digestible for the public, and serves as an educational tool highlighting the triumphs and environmental challenges of robotic interplanetary exploration.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used:

- Backend: Python, Django REST framework, SQLite

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js (Mapping), Chart.js (Telemetry Visualization)

- Development Environment: VS Code, Git/GitHub, AI-assisted code structuring tools

Creativity & Design Considerations:

Nebula Core avoids static placeholders by utilizing authentic time-series logs and physics equations. The UI replicates a professional NASA/JPL telemetry console using a dark space aesthetic (#0b0d17) with neon telemetry accents, blending rigorous science with compelling historical storytelling.
